beats.care: Every litre builders stop taking from the drinking supply is a litre that can reach homes, including yours, next summer.
beats.what: The water board, HMWSSB, will launch a Dial-a-Green Tanker service on 1 November, supplying treated sewage water for construction, industries and parks.
beats.why: Rain was weak, groundwater is falling and the Singur and Manjira reservoirs are under pressure, raising fears of a summer shortage.

cards.body: Managing director K. Ashok Reddy says the board wants 500 million litres a day of treated water used for non-drinking needs. A digital platform will match tankers with nearby treatment plants and track bookings.
Borewells that once struck water at 300 feet are failing far deeper, Telangana Today reports.
cards.caption: Depth where some borewells now run dry

cards.body: Hyderabad supplies about 150 litres per person a day, more than Bengaluru (108) or Chennai (135), yet still falls short of demand.

cards.q: Should builders be forced to use treated water?

opts: To save drinking water before summer
cards.q: Why is Hyderabad pushing treated water for builders?
cards.why: With weak rain and a supply gap, using treated water for construction leaves more clean water for homes.

hook: Hyderabad will truck *treated sewage water* to builders. Here's why

learn.t: Hyderabad's water board supplies about 585 million gallons a day against demand of about 735, a 150 MGD gap.

watch: Dial-a-Green Tanker launches on 1 November. Watch for the booking platform and prices, not yet announced.
